sources.full: Courneya KS et al., Structured Exercise after Adjuvant Chemotherapy for Colon Cancer, N Engl J Med 2025, PMID 40450658, https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2502760 | Moore SC et al., Leisure-Time Physical Activity and Risk of 26 Types of Cancer in 1.44 Million Adults, JAMA Intern Med 2016, PMID 27183032, https://doi.org/10.1001/jamainternmed.2016.1548

description:
Can exercise actually lower your cancer risk? In a big Canadian-led trial, a structured exercise plan cut colon cancer's comeback risk by about 28%. Cyto breaks it down from the 6ix.

What the trial did: 889 people who had finished surgery and chemo for stage III or high-risk stage II colon cancer were randomly assigned to a 3-year structured exercise program or health-education materials. After a median 7.9 years, disease-free survival (no recurrence, new primary cancer or death) was better with exercise (HR 0.72). At 5 years: 80.3% vs 73.9% disease-free. More muscle and joint injuries happened in the exercise group (18.5% vs 11.5%).

What the bigger picture says: pooling 12 cohorts (1.44 million adults), the most active people had lower risk of 13 of 26 cancers. That is a link, not proof, and melanoma and prostate cancer risk were slightly HIGHER in active people. The trial was in colon cancer patients, not healthy people.

Not medical advice. Talk to your care team before starting an exercise plan, especially during or after cancer treatment.

Not medical advice.
